evidence.claim: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.title: Know the PM
evidence.publisher: Prime Minister of India
evidence.excerpt: The official PMO biography states that Narendra Modi served as Prime Minister from 2019 to 2024, so he was in office throughout 2022.
evidence.source_locator: biography paragraph with the service dates
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography; direct office-tenure claim.
evidence.period_fit: Confirms officeholding during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes executive office to Modi, but not any specific nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: Promotional tone and no detail on nuclear authority or 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: The Union Budget 2022-23 set the fiscal deficit at 6.4% of GDP and stepped up capital expenditure by 35.4% to Rs 7.50 lakh crore, with effective capital expenditure at Rs 10.68 lakh crore.
evidence.title: Fiscal Deficit Estimated at 6.4% of GDP in 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Finance
evidence.excerpt: The Union Budget 2022-23 set the fiscal deficit at 6.4% of GDP and stepped up capital expenditure by 35.4% to Rs 7.50 lakh crore, with effective capital expenditure at Rs 10.68 lakh crore.
evidence.source_locator: headline and body paragraphs on fiscal deficit and capital expenditure
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government budget release with exact figures announced in Parliament.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 budget policy choice for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government through the Union Budget and Finance Ministry.
contrary_evidence: The fiscal deficit remained elevated, so the policy was pro-growth but not fiscally conservative in an absolute sense.
Budget announcements do not prove implementation on their own.

evidence.claim: By January 2023 the government said about 67% of the 2022-23 capital expenditure outlay had been spent by end-December 2022, alongside 8,964 National Infrastructure Pipeline projects and record road and waterways output.
evidence.title: Capital Expenditure Outlay for 2022-23 Increased Sharply by 35.4% with Approximately 67% Spent Between April-December 2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Finance
evidence.excerpt: By January 2023 the government said about 67% of the 2022-23 capital expenditure outlay had been spent by end-December 2022, alongside 8,964 National Infrastructure Pipeline projects and record road and waterways output.
evidence.source_locator: headline and opening paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation update with concrete execution figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective evidence on implementation of the 2022 budget within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s fiscal and infrastructure execution.
contrary_evidence: The source is a government self-report, so it may accentuate success.
It reports spending volume, not full welfare impact.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal measures to support vulnerable groups and front-loaded monetary tightening, with inflation projected at 6.9% in FY2022/23 and risks tilted down.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.publisher: International Monetary Fund
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal measures to support vulnerable groups and front-loaded monetary tightening, with inflation projected at 6.9% in FY2022/23 and risks tilted down.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and Executive Board Assessment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous IMF surveillance with explicit findings on policy response and macro conditions.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period macroeconomic assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Modi government and the RBI policy mix under its institutional framework; monetary policy is partly independent, fiscal measures are directly governmental.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also said public debt sustainability risks had increased.
The source shows stabilization efforts, not a fully successful macro environment.

evidence.claim: The IMF staff report said India’s world-class public digital infrastructure was facilitating innovation, productivity improvements and access to services, and that further structural reforms were needed for strong and sustainable growth.
evidence.title: India: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for India
evidence.publisher: International Monetary Fund
evidence.excerpt: The IMF staff report said India’s world-class public digital infrastructure was facilitating innovation, productivity improvements and access to services, and that further structural reforms were needed for strong and sustainable growth.
evidence.source_locator: Summary and staff report summary section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF country report with explicit causal language on digital infrastructure and reforms; still a surveillance document rather than an audit.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period structural-growth assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but real attribution to the Modi government because these digital-state capabilities and reform choices were national policy outputs.
contrary_evidence: The report frames these as enabling conditions, not as proof of broad-based welfare gains.
Structural reforms are recommended as still needed, so the record is unfinished.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said India’s growth for FY2022/23 was estimated at 6.9%, investment was bolstered by the government’s capex push, and inflation averaged around 6.7% for the year.
evidence.title: Indian Economy Continues to Show Resilience Amid Global Uncertainties
evidence.publisher: World Bank
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said India’s growth for FY2022/23 was estimated at 6.9%, investment was bolstered by the government’s capex push, and inflation averaged around 6.7% for the year.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and outlook table
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank India update with explicit growth, investment, and inflation figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly on the 2022-23 period that includes the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly attributable to the Modi government’s fiscal choices, though the outcome also reflects private demand and external conditions.
contrary_evidence: The same source says growth moderated in the second half of FY22/23.
Inflation remained elevated, so the outcome was resilient rather than fully comfortable.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $47 million project to support Mission Karmayogi and help build the functional and behavioral competencies of about four million civil servants.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $47 Million Program to Strengthen India’s Public Sector Capability
evidence.publisher: World Bank
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $47 million project to support Mission Karmayogi and help build the functional and behavioral competencies of about four million civil servants.
evidence.source_locator: press release body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank project approval with a concrete capacity-building target and clear 2022 date.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period institutional-capacity evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government because Mission Karmayogi is a national government program.
contrary_evidence: This is capacity-building rather than proof of better policy outcomes.
It speaks to state capability, not to direct competence of every economic appointment.

evidence.claim: The RBI said CPI inflation remained above the upper tolerance band for 10 successive months in 2022-23, and that government supply-side measures such as excise duty cuts and lower import duties, together with cumulative repo-rate tightening, helped contain price pressures.
evidence.title: Annual Report 2022-23
evidence.publisher: Reserve Bank of India
evidence.excerpt: The RBI said CPI inflation remained above the upper tolerance band for 10 successive months in 2022-23, and that government supply-side measures such as excise duty cuts and lower import duties, together with cumulative repo-rate tightening, helped contain price pressures.
evidence.source_locator: Economic Review, Inflation in India, and central government finances sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank annual report with explicit diagnosis and policy chronology.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the target year and fiscal year that includes 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly direct and partly institutional: government supply-side measures are directly attributable to Modi’s administration, while rate hikes were RBI decisions.
contrary_evidence: Inflation still exceeded the tolerance band for much of the year.
The report stresses that prices were driven by broad global and domestic shocks, not just domestic policy.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the RBI raised the repo rate to 6.25% in December 2022, the fifth straight increase, and said inflation remained elevated.
evidence.title: India central bank raises key rate, says inflation battle not over
evidence.publisher: ThePrint / Reuters
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the RBI raised the repo rate to 6.25% in December 2022, the fifth straight increase, and said inflation remained elevated.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on a major macro policy decision, widely corroborated by RBI records.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period monetary-policy evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution only: the RBI is operationally independent, though the government set the wider macro context.
contrary_evidence: The decision reflects central-bank independence as much as government direction.
Rate hikes are evidence of stabilization pressure, not of economic success.

evidence.claim: The ministry reported that under MGNREGA 11.37 crore households availed employment in 2022, and that 2.11 crore PMAY-G houses had been completed by mid-December 2022.
evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.excerpt: The ministry reported that under MGNREGA 11.37 crore households availed employment in 2022, and that 2.11 crore PMAY-G houses had been completed by mid-December 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Key Initiatives and Achievements section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end implementation report with concrete welfare-delivery figures.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period welfare and rural-income evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s rural-development delivery apparatus, though execution is shared with states.
contrary_evidence: Household employment under MGNREGA reflects distress as well as support.
The report is a government self-assessment.

evidence.claim: The government said 10.8 crore rural households had tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission by end-2022, and over 1 lakh villages were declared ODF Plus in 2022.
evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.excerpt: The government said 10.8 crore rural households had tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission by end-2022, and over 1 lakh villages were declared ODF Plus in 2022.
evidence.source_locator: headline and opening section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation report with concrete infrastructure-delivery figures.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period infrastructure evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s national infrastructure and service-delivery program, with implementation shared by states.
contrary_evidence: Tap-water coverage is a delivery metric, not direct proof of welfare gains.
ODF Plus status is an intermediate step, not a final development outcome.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that India’s factory activity expanded at a stronger pace in October 2022 and firms hired workers at the fastest pace in nearly three years, with the manufacturing PMI at 55.3.
evidence.title: India’s factory growth picks up speed in Oct, hiring at 33-month high
evidence.publisher: ThePrint / Reuters
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that India’s factory activity expanded at a stronger pace in October 2022 and firms hired workers at the fastest pace in nearly three years, with the manufacturing PMI at 55.3.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters survey report with a clear jobs and output signal.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period labour and manufacturing evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful attribution to the Modi government’s industrial and macro environment; the survey itself reflects private-sector activity.
contrary_evidence: The PMI is a survey, not a government administrative record.
It shows expansion and hiring, not job quality or income distribution.

evidence.claim: In a special address, the Prime Minister said PM GatiShakti was the first step toward integrated infrastructure planning, efficient coordination, and monitoring, and would reduce time and cost overruns in project execution; he also highlighted the central government's capex rise from Rs 2.5 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 7.5 lakh crore in 2022-23.
evidence.title: Enabling Logistics Efficiency through Implementation of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: In a special address, the Prime Minister said PM GatiShakti was the first step toward integrated infrastructure planning, efficient coordination, and monitoring, and would reduce time and cost overruns in project execution; he also highlighted the central government's capex rise from Rs 2.5 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 7.5 lakh crore in 2022-23.
evidence.source_locator: PIB summary of the PM's special address
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM speech reported by the government, with a specific policy mechanism and spending figure.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within February 2022 and describing the 2022 program baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Prime Minister and to his own stated program.
contrary_evidence: The speech and plan describe intended coordination; they do not by themselves prove later delivery.

evidence.claim: A written reply said project identification for PM Gati Shakti was ongoing using inputs from infrastructure and economic ministries, data layers were being integrated into the NMP portal, and the EGoS, NPG, and TSU had been constituted and operationalized.
evidence.title: Progress related to PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: A written reply said project identification for PM Gati Shakti was ongoing using inputs from infrastructure and economic ministries, data layers were being integrated into the NMP portal, and the EGoS, NPG, and TSU had been constituted and operationalized.
evidence.source_locator: bullet list in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official reply with concrete institutional details and clear 2022 date.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 rollout of the master plan.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Modi because it documents the implementation architecture of a flagship program launched under his government.
contrary_evidence: This shows rollout machinery, not actual project completion or outcome improvement by itself.

evidence.claim: The government said 1875 infrastructure projects were on the PMG portal, 5119 issues had been resolved for 1095 projects, and 634 projects still showed time overrun due to land acquisition, forest clearance, right of way, court cases, and similar constraints.
evidence.title: 1875 Projects are on Project Monitoring Group (PMG) Portal as on 28.07.2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The government said 1875 infrastructure projects were on the PMG portal, 5119 issues had been resolved for 1095 projects, and 634 projects still showed time overrun due to land acquisition, forest clearance, right of way, court cases, and similar constraints.
evidence.source_locator: headline and body summary in the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Concrete official monitoring statistics from a 2022 government monitoring platform.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year and directly about 2022 project execution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect to Modi: it reflects national project-monitoring under his administration, but the delays are also shaped by state-level and legal constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same release shows substantial unresolved delay, so the evidence is mixed rather than uniformly positive.

evidence.claim: The release says PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1900 GIS data layers for infrastructure mapping, over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined in the last year, and the master plan had expedited many previously stalled projects.
evidence.title: Shri Piyush Goyal reviews progress of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The release says PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1900 GIS data layers for infrastructure mapping, over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined in the last year, and the master plan had expedited many previously stalled projects.
evidence.source_locator: headline and summary paragraph in the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official progress review with specific quantitative indicators.
evidence.period_fit: Within the target year and directly about 2022 implementation progress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: it shows the program created under Modi was being used to coordinate and accelerate infrastructure execution in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Ministerial review evidence is still administrative self-reporting and does not independently verify project-level outcomes.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the DPL would support reforms critical to addressing financing gaps by leveraging private sector investment in infrastructure, small businesses, and green finance, and noted that India had improved financial inclusion and resilience over the prior decade.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $750 Million Loan to India to Catalyze Private Financing and Support Economic Growth
evidence.publisher: World Bank
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the DPL would support reforms critical to addressing financing gaps by leveraging private sector investment in infrastructure, small businesses, and green finance, and noted that India had improved financial inclusion and resilience over the prior decade.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral source describing a government reform package and its financing purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Modi's government program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Government of India under Modi, though the Bank also treats the reforms as part of a longer reform trajectory and not solely a personal initiative.
contrary_evidence: The loan supports reforms and financing; it does not by itself prove full implementation or final outcomes.

evidence.claim: As of 28.07.2022, 1,875 infrastructure projects were on the PMG portal; the government said it had resolved 5,119 issues pertaining to 1,095 projects, while 634 projects still showed time overruns due to land acquisition, forest clearance, right of way, right of use, and court cases.
evidence.title: 1875 Projects are on Project Monitoring Group (PMG) Portal as on 28.07.2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: As of 28.07.2022, 1,875 infrastructure projects were on the PMG portal; the government said it had resolved 5,119 issues pertaining to 1,095 projects, while 634 projects still showed time overruns due to land acquisition, forest clearance, right of way, right of use, and court cases.
evidence.source_locator: headline and body text of the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official monitoring statistics with concrete counts and named bottleneck categories.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly about project execution status.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the PMG system operated under Modi's government and reflects executive monitoring capacity; the delays also reflect state-level and legal constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same release reports substantial unresolved time overruns, so it is mixed rather than purely positive.

evidence.claim: The review said PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1,900 GIS data layers, that over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined in the last year, and that the plan had expedited many previously stalled projects.
evidence.title: Shri Piyush Goyal reviews progress of PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The review said PM GatiShakti had incorporated more than 1,900 GIS data layers, that over 250 infrastructure projects had been examined in the last year, and that the plan had expedited many previously stalled projects.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs 13-18 of the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific contemporaneous government progress report with quantitative implementation details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and squarely about implementation progress in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Modi's program: this is follow-through on a flagship mechanism launched under his government, though the review itself is ministerial rather than a personal PM act.
contrary_evidence: It remains a government self-report and does not independently audit project completion quality or durability.

evidence.claim: The government reduced the public-grievance redressal timeline from 45 days to 30 days, describing the change as consistent with Prime Minister Modi's emphasis on effective grievance disposal.
evidence.title: Grievance redressal timeline reduced from 45 days to 30 days
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
evidence.excerpt: The government reduced the public-grievance redressal timeline from 45 days to 30 days, describing the change as consistent with Prime Minister Modi's emphasis on effective grievance disposal.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted ministerial statement in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government policy change with a specific timeline adjustment and explicit linkage to the PM's stated administrative priority.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to administrative correction and follow-through.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the policy sits within Modi's governance style and administration, but it is not itself evidence that he personally replaced underperforming staff.
contrary_evidence: A shorter target is a process reform, not proof that service quality or outcomes fully improved.

evidence.claim: A task force was constituted to coordinate filling vacant posts under the recruitment plan after the Prime Minister's instruction to recruit 10 lakh people in mission mode, and CPGRAMS was made operational in all scheduled languages.
evidence.title: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh says, a Task Force has been constituted to coordinate the progress of filling up of the vacant posts as per the 'Recruitment Plan'
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
evidence.excerpt: A task force was constituted to coordinate filling vacant posts under the recruitment plan after the Prime Minister's instruction to recruit 10 lakh people in mission mode, and CPGRAMS was made operational in all scheduled languages.
evidence.source_locator: headline and first two paragraphs of the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific staffing and process response tied to a direct PM instruction, with clear 2022 timing.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly about staffing adaptation in response to a PM-directed target.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable at the level of executive direction: the PM set the recruitment target, and the ministry created a coordination mechanism to implement it; it still does not prove replacement of any specific ineffective official.
contrary_evidence: The release shows staffing correction, but not evidence that the government replaced a particular failed implementer.
